query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing an adaptive enhanced sampling strategy, such as replica exchange or metadynamics guided intermediate-state selection, into the thermodynamic integration framework will significantly improve reference–target phase-space overlap for the ab initio liquid in multicomponent high-entropy alloys, thereby reducing the thermodynamic integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both their solid and liquid states at or near their high melting temperatures, where the liquid phase has a vast array of atomic configurations.
generation.intervention: Implement an adaptive enhanced sampling method that dynamically selects and adjusts intermediate states during thermodynamic integration (e.g., via replica exchange or metadynamics).
generation.conditions: Applicable to high-entropy alloys composed of five or more metallic elements at temperatures near or above their high melting temperatures (approximately 2000 K to 3600 K), where liquid-state configurational diversity is prominent.
generation.structural_mediator: The dynamically generated intermediate atomic configurations that bridge the configurational gap between the simplified EAM reference ensemble and the complex ab initio liquid state.
generation.mechanism: By continuously adapting the sampling of the intermediate states, the enhanced sampling method more accurately represents the full ensemble of atomic configurations, thus ensuring a better overlap between the reference and target phase spaces. This should, in turn, reduce the integration-path mismatch because the reference system will better mirror the fluctuations and configurational diversity of the target liquid state.
generation.predicted_outcome: A measurable reduction in the mismatch of the thermodynamic integration path relative to the TOR-TILD approach; the free-energy convergence should be closer to the true ab initio values, with an expected improvement on the order of tens of percent in phase-space overlap efficacy, though the exact quantitative reduction remains uncertain.
generation.baseline: The current TOR-TILD method using conventional EAM references that inadequately capture the variety of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid state.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be most effective for equimolar multicomponent systems near their melting points. Its benefits may diminish for simpler binary systems or at considerably lower temperatures where the configurational landscape is less complex.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of the reduction in integration path mismatch is uncertain and will require focused free-energy benchmarking to quantify. Moreover, the performance of the adaptive strategy in systems with extreme compositional or phase-space characteristics is not yet established.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a representative equimolar high-entropy alloy system and perform two sets of thermodynamic integration calculations: one using the conventional TOR-TILD EAM references and one using the proposed adaptive enhanced sampling strategy. Compare the free energy curves, convergence metrics, and predicted melting properties against independent ab initio simulations and experimental benchmarks.
measurements: Free-energy differences along the integration path
Convergence rate and residual path mismatch
Experimental melting temperature and latent heat values
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the adaptive enhanced sampling approach does not produce a statistically significant improvement in phase-space overlap (as evidenced by a reduced free-energy integration mismatch and closer agreement with experimental free-energy benchmarks) compared to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Towards this, some inspiration has recently been taken from the field of metallurgy; in which the useful compositional space for the exploration of new alloys was drastically increased upon the discovery of High Entropy Alloys (HEAs),. These materials consist of single-phase crystalline solid solutions (crystallographic order), comprised of a random arrangement of >4 metallic components in near-equiatomic proportions (chemical disorder). Such compositions were previously expected to produce multiphase alloys, consisting of brittle intermetallics; and were therefore expected to be impractical for most applications. In reality, it was discovered that single-phase materials could be stabilised via their enhanced molar configurational entropy (ΔSmix = RlnN, where N is the number of equimolar components and R is the gas constant),, which minimises the Gibb’s free energy (G = H − TS, where H is enthalpy, S is entropy, and T is temperature) by boosting the –TS term. The –TS term becomes more dominant at elevated temperatures, suggesting that high entropy phases could be particularly stable at high temperatures. cited_evidence.text: To understand the origin of the Cr- and V-rich precipitates observed in annealed and irradiated HEA samples, we have systematically carried out first-principles calculations of phase stability and chemical short-range order (SRO) of the multicomponent 38 at % W/36 at % Ta/15 at % Cr/11 at % V alloy as a function of temperature. The cluster expansion (CE) methodology [see Methods and refs. ()] has been used to build up an ab initio–based Hamiltonian with many-body effective cluster interactions (ECIs), from which the configurational entropy and therefore the free energy of multicomponent system can be obtained from thermodynamic integration techniques () in combination with canonical Monte Carlo (CMC) simulations. The enthalpies of mixing were calculated using the density functional theory (DFT) and CE methods for nearly 270 structures within the BCC underlying crystalline lattice. Values for all binary structures in the database were analyzed to determine the nature of the atomic interactions in all possible binary configurations (fig. S7). The positive and negative enthalpies of mixing values indicate a tendency for segregation or ordering, respectively.

frame.system: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys in their solid and liquid states at and near high melting temperatures, where the liquid state exhibits a vast number of accessible atomic configurations.
frame.goal: Develop and test a methodological intervention that improves the phase‐space overlap between reference and target systems during thermodynamic integration, thereby reducing the mismatch in the integration path and improving free‐energy predictions.
frame.limitation: Existing EAM (Embedded Atom Method) references, such as those employed in TOR-TILD, are unable to account for the complexity and configurational diversity of the ab initio liquid state in high-entropy alloys, leading to significant thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
root_cause_cues: many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid
constraints: A single, testable, methodological intervention must be proposed
The intervention should yield a measurable reduction in integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references
It must include specifications for applicable composition and temperature ranges
The approach should be supported by evidence from previous elemental or binary calculations
A decisive free-energy benchmark is required that would falsify the hypothesis if not met
frame.regime: Near or at the high melting temperatures of the alloys, encompassing both the solid and liquid phases where the liquid phase is characterized by extensive configurational diversity.
prior_attempts: TOR-TILD utilizing EAM references, which, while successful in simpler systems, fails to capture the multi-component configurational complexity in the ab initio liquid state, leading to poor phase-space overlap and integration-path mismatch.

families.principle: Enhancing the thermodynamic integration framework through improved sampling methods which ensure robust phase‐space overlap between reference and target systems, thereby reducing integration-path mismatch.
cues_against: Existing TOR-TILD using EAM references already uses a sampling scheme that fails in highly complex configurational landscapes
families.best_lever: Implement an adaptive, enhanced sampling strategy (e.g., replica exchange or metadynamics guided intermediate-state selection) within the thermodynamic integration protocol to dynamically optimize phase‐space overlap.

families.principle: Utilizing machine learning to construct potentials or sampling frameworks that learn from ab initio data, enabling faithful reproduction of the energy landscape and configurational diversity of multicomponent alloys.
cues_against: The intervention must be a single, testable methodological approach and integration into thermodynamic integration protocols may require extra validation steps
families.best_lever: Deploy a neural network potential trained on diverse ab initio liquid state configurations to serve as a reference that directly enhances phase‐space overlap during thermodynamic integration.

families.principle: Developing an improved interatomic potential that inherently captures the many‐body effects and configurational diversity of multicomponent systems—moving beyond the limitations of conventional EAM formulations.
cues_for: many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid
cues_against: THER-TILD’s design already uses an interatomic potential approach, so simply modifying the potential might not address phase‐space overlap issues if sampling remains inadequate
families.best_lever: Introduce a higher‐fidelity potential (for example, a machine-learned correction to EAM) that is specifically calibrated on ab initio liquid configurations for high-entropy alloys.

families.principle: Employing experimental techniques to directly measure free-energy differences and validate computational predictions, thereby providing an independent benchmark.
cues_against: the focus on methodological intervention is computational and aimed at improving simulation reference systems
families.best_lever: Develop a high-temperature calorimetric method to measure free-energy changes in situ for high-entropy alloys, although this is less central given the simulation focus.
